thread:
incident-bot: P1 alert - prod-us-central: high GPU queue depth + tail latency for model redwood-35b. Dash: https://dash.internal/r/xyz. Errors: OOM evictions x50 in last 5m.

maria.k: I'm paged, joining. seeing queue_depth ~120, p99 ~2.1s, p95 ~420ms. autoscale hasn't scaled up for last 10m.

aj: confirmed. scaling events are queued; pool g-3 at 98% GPU mem. Some requests show very long prefix cache misses.

samir: initial thought — throughput shortfall because many short requests are getting stuck behind a few huge seq-length jobs. We can either throttle large seq jobs or increase batching window to boost overall throughput.

\maria.k: quick mitigation proposals: 1) apply soft rate limit to free-tier (limit=5r/s) 2) bump continuous_batch_max_delay_ms from 10 -> 50 to form bigger batches (more throughput, worse tail latency) 3) cap single-request tokens to 2048 for now. Thoughts?

aj: roll 1 and 3 now. Rolling batching change might worsen p99 for interactive users, but will reduce queue and lower error/OOMs. recommend doing 1+3 immediately, then test 2 on a single region.

leo: running ACL patch to apply route-level throttle for routes: /api/v1/generate (tenant: free-tier). Command: 
```bash
opsctl routes update --route "/api/v1/generate" --tier free --rate 5r/s --burst 10
```

ops-bot: Route update queued, patch-id=patch-8932, will apply in 6s.

ops-bot: Patch patch-8932 applied to prod-us-central.

samir: applying cap on request tokens via feature-flag. patch-id=cap-2048.

ops-bot: Feature-flag cap-2048 active (scope: prod-us-central).

maria.k: now testing batching change on canary subset (10% of traffic) — bump continuous_batch_max_delay_ms 10->50 and max_batch_tokens 256->512. Patch below:
```json
{ "continuous_batch_max_delay_ms": 50, "max_batch_tokens": 512 }
```

aj: metrics after 2min on canary: throughput +42%, avg GPU util up 15%, queue_depth canary down from 110 -> 18, p95 increased 420ms -> 610ms, p99 increased 2.1s -> 3.6s. OOMs on canary dropped to 0.

maria.k: Can confirm. Canary stable, no errors. Given severity, I'm approving roll to full region but only while free-tier throttle remains. This trades higher p99 for fewer OOMs and restores capacity for paid customers. Rolling in 30s.

ops-bot: Rolling batch-config patch to prod-us-central (patch-id=batch-4467). Staged rollout: 10% -> 100% over 60s.

anya: taking over on-call for next 2h. I'm on audio, ping me for handoff notes.

leo: rolling completed. Post-roll metrics: global throughput +38%, overall queue_depth went from 120 -> 22, OOMs suppressed. Customer-facing error rate down 1.8% -> 0.2%. p95 up modestly, p99 up as seen on canary.

maria.k: action items logged: 
- Short term: keep free-tier rate limit & token cap for 2 hours.
- Mid term: run prompt-length retry stratification and add requester-side token estimation.
- Postmortem: investigate autoscale latency and kernel memory fragmentation.

samir: adding note: revert batch window back to 10ms when traffic normalizes, or add dynamic policy that reduces batch delay for interactive routes.

anya: handoff ack. I'll watch metrics and will revert if p99 impacts key enterprise customers. Contact list pinned.

maria.k: marking incident: mitigated. leaving monitoring for 30m then close. Revert planned at end of watch window unless issues.

ops-bot: Scheduled revert job (if no regressions) at timestamp 3467894010 to revert continuous_batch_max_delay_ms -> 10 and remove free-tier throttle.

leo: copying quick runbook snippet here for future on-call: 
- If OOMs spike + queue>80: 1) enable route throttle for low-priority, 2) cap tokens, 3) run canary of increased batch window, 4) roll if stable.

maria.k: incident closed (mitigated) at 3467890410. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
